subject: OptiPay - availability reconciliation & SLA exception request
messages:
From: Sasha Torres <sasha@optipay.com>

Date: Sat, 08 May 2027 21:15:00 -0700
Subject: Intermittent 503s during payment auth window — please confirm downtime and credit eligibility

Hi Mina,

We saw a spike of 503s during our critical batch of payment authorizations tonight (roughly 21:03–21:20 PDT). The failures impacted ~3% of authorization requests and correspond to retries on our side that caused customer-facing decline notices.

Can you confirm whether this is reflected on Redwood's side as an availability gap? Our contracts reference a 99.95% availability SLA for payment endpoints and we need to understand whether this qualifies for a credit and an RCA/postmortem.

I've attached a short CSV with a sample of failed request IDs and timestamps, plus an initial trace (optipay-snippet.log) — full trace bundle available on request. Please let me know:
- confirmation of the downtime window you see
- what data you'll provide for evidence (raw traces, routing decisions, topology events)
- expected timeline for a postmortem and credit calculation

We're under time pressure to communicate to our legal and billing teams, so appreciate a quick confirmation.

Thanks,
Sasha Torres
Ops Lead, OptiPay Inc.
[sent from phone]

- optipay-snippet.log (text, 45KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 08:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent 503s during payment auth window — OptiPay (triage results)

Mina / team,

I pulled the traces and correlated telemetry. Short summary below (full bundle attached):

- Confirmed availability gap: 2027-05-08T21:03:12Z through 2027-05-08T21:20:45Z (approx. 17m 33s).
- Root symptom: transient routing instability in us-west-2 induced by a control-plane scheduler race during a pool reconfiguration. Multiple requests were briefly routed to a pool that was mid-warmup and returned 503s until KV-cache priming completed.
- Impact: ~2.7% of requests to OptiPay's production route returned 503. Successful fallback to a smaller model variant occurred after ~90s for most sessions, but a subset of short-lived requests did not retry in time.
- Mitigations performed: automatic pool fallback triggered; on-call issued rollback of the reconfiguration at 21:22Z. Ticket tracking: INC-20270508-874 (created 21:09Z).

Attachments included: optipay_raw_traces_20270508.zip (raw front-end + router + scheduler logs), scheduler-events-20270508.txt (extract), and a short excerpt of matching request IDs. I created a short timeline (text file) that maps scheduler events to client timestamps.

SLA assessment: based on the confirmed window and the contract's definition of "availability," this appears to qualify as an availability gap. Final credit calculation depends on per-route usage during the window (Grace can compute that from the billing snapshot). I recommend we:
1) Assemble the evidence bundle for OptiPay (raw traces + timeline + scheduler event CSV).
2) Offer a prorated credit per the contract (we'll compute % of downtime and apply to billed units for that period).
3) Offer a written postmortem within 5 business days and a short remediation plan (scheduler hardening + improved warmup gating).

I'll attach the raw bundles to the reply to Sasha once Grace confirms the billing snapshot.

-David

--
David Kim
Senior Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference
[david.kim@redwood.com]

Date: Sun, 09 May 2027 17:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent 503s during payment auth window — confirmation and next steps

Hi Sasha — thanks for the sample and for flagging this quickly.

We've completed an initial validation and can confirm an availability gap affecting OptiPay's production route on 2027-05-08 from 21:03:12 UTC through 21:20:45 UTC (approx. 17 minutes 33 seconds). The engineering analysis indicates this was caused by a routing/scheduler reconfiguration that temporarily routed requests to a pool that was still warming up; fallback protections reduced impact but did not prevent a subset of requests from getting 503s.

What we'll provide next (by EOD tomorrow unless you need it sooner):
- Evidence bundle: raw traces, scheduler event log, and a mapped timeline (link: https://drive.redwood.com/optipay/trace-bundle-20270508).
- Preliminary credit estimate: Grace is preparing a billing snapshot for May 8 that we'll use to compute a prorated credit under the SLA.
- Postmortem: technical RCA + remediation plan (target delivery: 5 business days).

If you'd like a shorter turnaround for the postmortem, we can provide an executive summary within 48 hours and a full technical write-up in 5 business days. Please confirm which you prefer, and whether you want Redwood to open a formal credit request ticket we can route to billing/legal.

We appreciate the heads-up and will keep you updated on the timeline.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Account Manager, Enterprise
